I like the game... BUT There's a serious lack of progression and meaningful gameplay. The loop so far is "play to unlock new characters + skins + trinkets" and that's it. There's nothing that changes between games except the core skills that each character have. I think it also wouldn't take a lot to actually spice up the progression, like: add meta upgrades; add the ability to evolve skills (as is seen in most game of this genre and makes each run unique, even with the same characters); add challenges; add unlocks like new weapons and passives. There are so many minor changes that could be made to make this game a lot more fun. I've put 4 hours into this game and feel done, but have spent 200+ in Vampire Survivors, even though there are so many similarities. I wish the devs would look at what makes that game (which basically jumpstarted this genre) work and where this game falls short.

Honestly great game especially with friends, however coop may feel a little start-stopy with the amount of upgrade menu each player has to go through, (Just two players at lvl 100+ you are sitting through around 200 menus just on one run.) Suggestion for this is just make exp shared and change elixir into a global perk for the team so everyone levels up and go through the selection of upgrades together. Maybe rebalance or buff powerups / upgrades to be stronger in each upgrade selection in exchange for rebalancing/ tweaking exp curve so that players level up less frequently the longer the run goes. Overall besides the upgrade menu issues in coop, game is solid and would recommend.

This game is in early access, so take everything written below with a grain of salt. This negative review isn't a reaction to an obviously unfinished product - which by the way, is clearly a labor of love. It's a reaction to recent changes that show the rather unfortunate direction. "Mobmania" is a very difficult game. Even in co-op (two to four players). This difficulty however doesn't stem from some deep, interesting gameplay. What makes this game hard are mostly three components: 1) Grind 2) Randomness of upgrades - a staple of this type of game, but some items in "Mobmania" are clearly much better than the others. Get them early enough and it's smooth sailing. Get them late, you're pretty much done, especially with weaker/support characters. 3) Confusing visuals - art is lovely, but there's so many colors and mobs (some really small) and with how many of those can gather around you, sometimes it's really difficult to see what you're doing. Another problem is pausing during upgrades - each player has separate XP meter, so every time they level up (which is frequent) the game pauses. You can turn that option off, but it doesn't really change the issue, does it? Now you can die during upgrading process, if you don't click fast enough, because you're not immune to damage and there's usually dozens of mobs around you. What's the solution? Well, according to devs is nerfing XP by 50%. Does it make sense with game that is already incredible challenging? I would say no, but the answer is: there are players who already beat this game with every character on single player and then there are groups who don't even have singe win, yada, yada. Yes. Of course there will be a percent of players who will get so good at the game, they will beat it even against all odds. Those are probably players, that are especially active on Discord/in community, so their voice is heard. However, most players are not going to invest hours upon hours in an extremely grindy game, with no overall progression system, just to beat one or two levels. Especially with halved XP. [b]Tl;dr:[/b] Game is heading in worrisome direction, where increasing difficulty doesn't stem from interesting or challenging gameplay, but from artificially making upgrades less frequent and therefore extending the grind. Halving enemies HP is a semi-solution, but doesn't change the fact, that the game, in that state, is just not fun to play. Neither for single player or bigger group.

作为一个从抢先测试开始玩到现在的玩家，对游戏做个粗浅的评价 1.游戏难度偏高，属于类吸血鬼幸存者游戏中难度最高那一档的，原因是每局游戏获得的金币可以购买新角色和皮肤，但并不能提高角色本身的属性和能力值，所以即便玩了很久，也没法像多数同类型的肉鸽游戏那样爽快的割草。更长的游戏时长能提高的仅是玩家的操作和游戏策略，而非角色本身。虽然这样保持了游戏的挑战性，但是对一些操作不那么好或者期望前期受苦后期无双的玩家就很不友好。 2.角色很多但平衡性并不好。到2.28为止，可用角色共有26个，个人在游戏过程中感觉“好用”的仅有忍者Jpec、毒师Karissa、火法师Amber、剑客Lucy、宽刃剑客Kristina、召唤师Julia、咖啡白领Dan。 忍者初始技能比较优秀，有单体多次攻击的忍镖、可以穿过敌人的巨型手里剑、提高攻击频率的影分身和可以抵挡伤害并且影遁提高移速的替身术，可以称之为综合能力最强的亲儿子，我前80小时刷钱买全角色和全皮肤几乎都是在用他。 毒师单体伤害不行，胜在毒的范围伤害和毒云的范围内无敌，提高急速等级的情况下可以接近无缝衔接，生存能力比较强。 剑客Lucy，伤害值扛把子，暴伤和普攻堆全了能打出接近1000的单次伤害，和其他角色可怜的破百伤害都不容易比起来真的很壮观。 宽刃剑客虽然伤害值没有剑客高，但是有剑气的范围伤害和生命值提高的自体天赋，生存能力强于剑客。 召唤师输出全靠粉红小弟围上去一阵群殴，单个输出不高但是数量贼多，激励技能发动的时候能对BOSS造成可观伤害。 咖啡白领单体伤害奇低，但是伤害范围大，配合通用技能里的红酒范围减速和自带天赋的喝咖啡提高输出频率，也能很好的清掉敌方小兵。 但是其他的角色性能就不太突出甚至是难用了，尤其是近战，很多近战角色在非挑战模式想正常通关都并不容易，我为了实现全角色拿王冠，某些特别难用的近战角色甚至不得不用逃跑大法硬拖时间，拖小BOSS到20分钟自己消失，再和关底的魔女BOSS慢慢熬。有时候运气不好拿不到增伤技能或者合适的通用技能，就会陷入“清不掉小兵--->拣不到经验球--->升不了级--->清不掉小兵--->拣不到经验球”的恶性循环。如果再去玩挑战模式，遇上BOSS或者小兵加强的是体型和伤害，那这种弱势角色就更是早早就会寄掉（跑跑不过，打打不掉）。 3.2月25号之后更新了Party和Badges系统，打挑战模式给的绿币有了用处，Party就是用自己手头的角色组个最多四人的队，每个角色给全队加通用属性，角色不同加的属性有所不同，属性还分T1-T4四个等级，每个角色通关5局提升一层属性，升到T4满属性需要单个角色通关20局，26个角色全刷满总计得打通关520局（囧）。比较尬的一点是花了这么多精力去刷，每个等级提升的属性非常有限，比如召唤师Julia，T1提升1攻，T2提升1防，花大把时间打通20局游戏，升满到T4也就总共提高2攻2防，投入巨大回报甚微。 再说Badges系统，用绿币可以买徽章，1级徽章1绿币，2级3绿币，3级5绿币，一个背包上限目前能装20点的徽章，1级2点，2级4点，3级6点，且同属性技能无法直接叠加，而是2+2，4+4，6+6（例如1级提高攻击范围1%的徽章上限可以获得4个，你装备四个就不是2点背包值，而是2*4=8点），对角色的提升微弱，而且加了20点的限制卡住，让玩家属性没法大幅提高。所以纵使给角色加上了组队获得的通用属性增益和背包徽章，整体上来讲也就略微比没上述两个系统加强前稍微强那么一丢丢，能打过的不加强也能打过，打不过的加强那点也还是打不过，用那些弱势角色依旧会突然暴毙，或者陷入打不过被耗死的死循环。 所以游戏总体还算好玩，但是接受不了受苦的玩家或者只想爽爽割草的玩家，我个人不建议入手，毕竟玩起来真的有点折磨的 PS：3月2日追加一些个人看法 这两天对游戏的Party和Badges进行了一点研究后，发现自己在2.28说的“两个新增系统对弱势角色提升微弱”的说法有失偏颇。 我在打了几十局挑战模式后，用绿币购买了4个增加3%攻击范围的徽章和2个增加1%攻击范围的徽章，再加上Party系统中，将冰电法师Jamie的友谊增幅刷到了T4，增加了8%的攻击范围，总体提升了22%的通用角色攻击范围。 这22%的角色通用范围提升一下就改变了游戏体验，之前被我认为属于一般或者弱鸡的角色脱颖而出一下都变为了强力角色。 例如上边举例的冰电法师Jamie，龙卷风多段伤害，电击圈范围控制有效防止怪物突脸，地面结冰大范围降低怪物移动速度，再加上自身还有3级的攻击范围提升和大范围的生命值持续回复，总体上攻防兼备还有较强的续航恢复能力，直接一跃成为顶级战力。 还有薙刀眼镜妹Ana，之前属于完全上不了台面的角色，现在装备通用的2点回血技能和自带的5点回血技能，配合通用冷却，再带一个任意治疗值加1的饰品，可以实现每3秒左右回复9点生命的固定值，再把吸血点出来更是如虎添翼，只要不是停着不动和怪物站撸，基本不存在死掉的可能性，自带的猫猫印记还能提高经验值获取，不带加5%经验饰品不点通用经验值技能的情况下也能单局达到78级左右，可以说比其他角色多出了两个MAX技能。 还有咖啡妹Reanne，把角色自带技能一点，再拿到悠悠球、杂志、花瓣、绿瓶烧酒，把通用冷却点满，就差不多可以停在那站撸了，除了关底的小魔女得走下位，其他多数BOSS活不过5秒。 目前依旧觉得不太好用的角色有技术工人Kris、飞剑客Alex、吸血鬼Draco、机器人Ray、画家Paige、刺客Yifan，需要进一步研究一下适合他们角色技能特性的各种搭配。 总而言之多数角色比更新系统之前还是好打很多了

The strongest reason to purchase this game over any other in its genre is that it has online multiplayer. The online multiplayer is effectively ruined on account of asynchronous levelups spam pausing the game. Only a singular character has a significant increased XP mechanic, and could easily be changed to an increased item from XP passive with no change in playstyle. Despite this, the devs have apparently taken a hard line stance against this change and have locked multiple threads of fans asking for it without explanation. So what would be the most compelling aspect of the game is moot, and it isn't going to change no matter how obvious the problem and simple the solution is.

【tl;dr: Low replayability for a VS-style game, run customisation almost nonexistent. Worth the price? Debatable.】 Fun and cool characters, but no evolutions/combinations for weapons. Also, having to take random weapons because you've already maxed out your character's unique upgrades so early really sucks. In HoloCure (the obvious comparison), characters have clear identities, with most having huge or really powerful abilities. In MobMania, *most* characters have tiny abilities that can't really hold up on their own damage-wise. Some, like the shadow clone, poison spread and minion controller characters are pretty unique, but they don't reflect the general quality of the roster. The biggest issue I have is with the common weapon upgrades. They suck. They're really uninteresting thematically, have no evolutions and do so little damage you usually just have to dilute your build by taking a ton of them. There's also so few of them that you'll have tried all of them after 1-2 runs. Coop doesn't have shared XP, and you have two choices to deal with the staggered level ups: 1. Game pauses for the other player each time one of you levels up. 2. The game never pauses, but you aren't invulnerable while selecting upgrades. This is super questionable. Maybe the devs just expect the player to play without pause and know every upgrade they want, but even then a poorly timed level up can just kill you. The biggest selling point of MobMania is its maps and bosses, which are varied and really well designed. The exception to this is the ranged bunny boss, which is nearly unkillable for certain melee characters. The vegetable that just sprints at you as a dps check also isn't very fun, but it's much more palatable than the bunny staying alive for 5+ minutes. This was fun for a little while, but quickly got really tedious. Worth a look, but it won't be one of my go-to VS-style games until there is way more run customisation.

This game is not like a lot of other games in this genre. It's doesn't have a gentle progression after upgrading stats and proceeding further into the game. This is a very skill based game. You are required to learn the patterns of the enemies and bosses, as well as learn which attacks and passives to pick and upgrade. It's hard at first, but once you figure things out the fun intensifies. After you've learned how to play the game and can regularly beat the final boss and complete the stages can you start with the meta progression in the game. This is all by design. The developers wanted to do something a little different from the norm. I admit I struggled with it at first, but once I started to figure things out I really started to enjoy the game. The game has a super cute look which can be quite deceiving. It's not as chill a game as a lot of the games in this genre/sub-genre. You really have to work for those wins at times. Once you figure things out though it becomes routine. I wouldn't call it a Souls-like because it doesn't play anything like one, but I would say it's one of those games that requires skill and for the player to be paying attention. The game is both easier and harder when playing with teammates. It all depends on how well you work together as a team. If you stick close together you should have an easier time of things. In the end I have to say that this is one of my favorite games in this genre despite my preference for games I can just sit back and chill with. I appreciate the challenge I guess.

This game deserves more love than it gets. It's very similar to vibe as HoloCure. The depth and complexity is crazy if you want to dedicate time to this. Nice art and gameplay feels smooth. All of the characters are interesting and have mechanics unique to the genre, for example there's an American Football character who attacks with footballs and you have to retreive them when it's thrown, you can summon linemen to help you out. There's a fisherman character who has an interesting cast and bobber mechanic. There's a new billiards character who shoots huge billiard balls. The attacks you have access to on all chracters are interesting and fun too, like a camera with a flash that stuns enemies. The only thing annoying about this game is it can be pretty grindy, there's one meta progression currency to unlock everything. Characters, skins, augments, cards, even cosmetics for the house you can chill in. It can be overwhelming with all the different systems knowing what to invest in, while still not having all the characters unlocked, for example. There's also some serious design bloat.
